searchText: **AllCoreDevs in 25 minutes** Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/365 Stream: https://youtu.be/jNxAB3WpAD0 Zoom: https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/91348592283?pwd=SnRnL1VTeXNYVE9CaWpBbnJEUXhQZz09 was it the shortest ACD ever? Yes 🙂 ... NFTs for everyone? Ah shoot, totally forgot 🙂 everyone is still flabbergasted by how much of non-event London ended up being 🙂 (problems-wise) 🙏 Thank you again to the devs for incredible execution. You let us just have a chill day of celebration 🙃 Yes, the ECH is celebrating with distributing London upgrade NFTs to as much as 100 contributors. Along with people involved with documenting notes, coordination process, the list contains every co-author of all 5 proposals, 5 for each client team, editors and many other who contributed in one way or the other. Our team has already started distributing NFTs with the public wallet available and reaching individuals. If you know someone who is missed, please reach me, <@!641438053059264512> , <@!601063305070772244> on Discord. Thanks! some miners are not filling blocks <@!489256758989029405> what do you mean? That the block gas used is very variable, or that miners are leaving potentially valid transactions in the mempool? second probably but we will need more data The basefee step feels too big (hard to ignore as a user). Any particular reason for such value? <@!425274498732916736> we discussed this on ACD this AM, and the short answer is "not really". We probably want a value where it quickly becomes prohibitive to spam the network (e.g. we can't have a 1% increase), but it may be worth making it smaller by, say, half? It would be great to have people analyse this in more depth, and client teams said on ACD if we found a better parameter that was a "one line change", we could change it alongside the difficulty bomb delay in December Yes, I think this also needs much more digging into. A very crude first metric would be to get data on the minimum, non-0, priority fee accepted by various miners Why do you think the second? And do you think this is any different from normal (pre London) empty blocks that we saw pre-London? On that note, maybe something that depends on more history/historical blocks? No idea how hard that would be to implement though (with short reorgs and all) https://etherscan.io/tx/0x368eeba20ac349b5d245a53d568eb5d0285dc60dd8f236a00c472e837d9cd600 Attempt to create a contract starting with 0xfe. I am curious why it was decided to burn all gas rather than just revert with gas spent? Because it is implemented the same way invalid instruction / bad jumpdest / `INVALID` are. Those were never changed to not consume all gas, only `REVERT` does that. We actually measured (not connected to this) how much we could "save" in a block with not consuming all gas in those cases, and it is not too much at this point as everyone uses `revert`, so only super broken cases end up with that. Super broken cases and my test-in-production. 😢 Your donation is much appreciated 🙏 Who do I send my receipts to for a refund? To the masternode? Isn't this actually just a contract creation transaction with `0xef` as **initcode**? Gah, it is. 😢 Unfortunately I already deleted the code I wrote to submit that transaction, and for reasons entirely unrelated to the `0xef` byte I'm now angry at software and refuse to write it again. Well, at least I'm helping to contribute to the burn. 😬 This was discussed before but IMO it’s best for it to be trivially calculated from the previous block header "0x600180600b6000396000f3ef" should work, can be manually sent from https://app.mycrypto.com/deploy-contracts it refuses to generate a tx, which means gas estimation fails.

excerpts.author: timbeiko
excerpts.content: <@!425274498732916736> we discussed this on ACD this AM, and the short answer is "not really". We probably want a value where it quickly becomes prohibitive to spam the network (e.g. we can't have a 1% increase), but it may be worth making it smaller by, say, half? It would be great to have people analyse this in more depth, and client teams said on ACD if we found a better parameter that was a "one line change", we could change it alongside the difficulty bomb delay in December
